interface.title: qPCR Melt Curve Viewer
interface.field: Molecular biology / qPCR (SYBR/TB Green melt-curve analysis)
interface.stage_of_work: Post-run quality control and documentation of qPCR melt-curve exports
interface.what_it_is_for: Load melt-curve and melt-peak text exports, pair them per well automatically, look at replicate curves and −dF/dT peaks side by side, remove outlier replicates, normalize, smooth or average the curves, and export the plots. Scope: this tree covers the Streamlit app only. The reviewer reports that the README recommends a standalone HTML version with an all-wells mean ± SD overlay, separate curve/peak Y-axis scaling and a combined long PNG. None of those were explored here.

data.note: Most of the run used 'Load sample data', which gives two wells (W1_7+5notail_ec_TBgreen and W2_sample_ec_TBgreen), each with 3 replicates (B8, C8, D8) and paired curve and peak files. I also uploaded the four test TXT files; they paired the same way. I then removed W2's peak file to see a 'curve_only' well. In this data the curves rise with temperature and the peaks point downward (negative). Because of that the Summary always shows Tm '—' and 'Peaks Detected' 0. Hovering on the plot shows each replicate's peak, for example D8 at 82.59 °C.

features.name: Automatic curve/peak file pairing with pairing table
features.general: Bring in a set of data files, match the two files that belong to each sample by name, and show a table of what was matched, with a status and similarity score so missing partners stand out
features.specific: Upload TXT/TSV/ZIP files or Load sample data, press Scan / Refresh, and read the Pairing table (paired / curve_only, Similarity, Curve File, Peak File). Paired wells feed the well selector. Only TXT files were tried; ZIP scanning was not exercised.
steps: Upload files (or load the sample set)
Press Scan / Refresh and read the counts message
Expand Pairing table to check each sample's status and matched files
Re-scan after adding or removing files to see the status change (e.g. curve_only)
serves_tasks: Load an example dataset and scan it
Upload your own data files and scan them
Check which data files were matched to each sample

features.name: Filterable sample multiselect driving plots and summary
features.general: Narrow a long list of samples with a text filter, pick several, and have the summary table and plots update to show only those
features.specific: Search / filter wells text box plus the Select wells multiselect (labels carry pairing status). Selection drives the Summary rows and the per-well plot pairs. Changing the filter cleared the per-well exclusion lists.
steps: Type part of a name in Search / filter wells
Add or remove wells as chips in Select wells
Read the updated Summary table and plot list

features.name: Side-by-side raw curve and derivative plot with hover readout
features.general: For each sample, draw the raw signal and its derivative next to each other with one trace per repeat, so the user can see whether there is one peak or several, hover to read a trace's identity and coordinates, or drag a box to zoom
features.specific: Per-well Plotly figure: Melt Curve (Fluorescence vs Temperature) and Melt Peak (−dF/dT vs Temperature). Hover shows the replicate well (e.g. D8), temperature and value; box zoom, then double-click to reset. All replicates share one legend entry and colour.
steps: Scroll to a well's plot pair
Hover a trace to read replicate ID, temperature and value
Drag a box to zoom into the peak or transition
Double-click to zoom back out
serves_tasks: Compare the raw curve and its derivative for each sample, check for one peak versus several (specificity), and read off the peak position

features.name: Display transforms: normalize and smooth
features.general: Switch on optional transforms that rescale each trace to a 0–100% range and smooth noisy traces, applied to both the raw and derivative plots
features.specific: Plot options toggles: Normalize curves (0–100%) (curve axis becomes Fluorescence (%)) and Savitzky–Golay smoothing. Both apply to the curve and peak plots.
steps: Toggle Normalize curves to put all wells on a 0–100% axis
Toggle Savitzky–Golay smoothing
Compare the rescaled, smoothed traces across wells
serves_tasks: Rescale each curve to a common 0–100% range

features.name: Replicate mean with ±1 SD band
features.general: Collapse the repeats of each sample into a mean line with a ±1 SD shaded band to show their spread. The SD band only becomes available once averaging is on.
features.specific: Plot options toggles Average replicates (adds a black Average trace) and ±1 SD shading (grey band; disabled until averaging is on). Applies to both the curve and peak plots and respects excluded replicates.
steps: Toggle Average replicates to add a black mean trace
Toggle ±1 SD shading
Box-zoom into the transition to see the spread
serves_tasks: Overlay the mean of the repeats with a ±1 SD band

features.name: Replicate outlier screening with manual override
features.general: Flag repeat measurements that disagree with their group, by hand or automatically by distance between curves (with an automatic or user-set threshold). The flags appear as an editable exclusion list per sample, and the exclusions carry through to the plots, averages, summary counts and exports. An automatic method based on shift in peak position is offered but was never shown to flag anything.
features.specific: Outlier removal: Enable switch; Method = Manual replicate selection / Automatic by curve deviation (Auto threshold 2.5× MAD on RMSE, or a set Outlier RMSE threshold) / Automatic by peak Tm deviation (Tm deviation threshold °C). Each well gets an 'Exclude — <well>' multiselect, pre-filled by the curve-deviation method when it flags something. The excluded replicates are listed under each plot, and the Summary Replicates count drops. On this data the auto MAD threshold flagged nothing, and the peak Tm method flagged nothing at any threshold, probably because no Tm is computed.
steps: Switch on Enable outlier removal
Choose Manual replicate selection or Automatic by curve deviation
For the automatic method, keep the auto threshold or untick it and type an RMSE threshold
Review and edit the pre-selected chips in each well's Exclude list
Check the 'Excluded replicates' caption, the lower Replicates count, and the export contents
serves_tasks: Flag bad repeats automatically by how far each curve is from the others
Adjust the automatically flagged list by hand

features.name: Per-sample summary table
features.general: Show one row per selected sample with its number of repeats after exclusions, its peak position, the number of peaks found and its pairing status
features.specific: Summary table (Sample, Replicates, Tm (°C), Peaks Detected, Status). Replicates follows the exclusion lists. On this data (negative-going peaks) Tm always showed '—' and Peaks Detected 0, so the table never reported a peak call. A curve_only well shows Replicates 0 even though its plot shows 3. The CSV download icon gave no file.
steps: Select the wells to summarize
Read Replicates and check it drops after excluding outliers
Read Tm and Peaks Detected (stayed '—'/0 on this data)
Read Status for each well
serves_tasks: Read the per-sample summary of replicate counts and peak calls

features.name: Multi-format batch plot export
features.general: Choose output formats with checkboxes, then either write one file per sample per format or download one combined interactive report that reflects the current exclusions and display settings
features.specific: Export checkboxes PNG / PDF / HTML. 'Export all selected wells' writes melt_plot_N files to a server temp folder and lists the paths; in this setup only HTML worked, and PNG/PDF failed with 'RuntimeError: Kaleido requires Google Chrome to be installed'. 'Download combined HTML' saves melt_plots.html in the browser. The chart's camera icon saves a single PNG. A 'Download first well (PNG)' button never appeared, since it depends on server-side image export.
steps: Tick the formats wanted (HTML worked; PNG and PDF failed here)
Press Export all selected wells and read the listed file paths
Press Download combined HTML for a single interactive file
Optionally use the plot camera icon for a one-off PNG
serves_tasks: Write per-sample plot files in the chosen formats
Save one figure as an image from the chart itself

screens_never_reached: A Summary table with a numeric Tm and Peaks Detected > 0: with this sample data (negative peaks) Tm always showed '—' and Peaks Detected 0, under every setting I tried
Automatic by peak Tm deviation actually flagging a replicate: nothing was flagged even at 0.05 °C, presumably because no Tm was detected
Pairing table states other than 'paired' and 'curve_only' (e.g. peak-only or low-similarity pairs), and the ZIP-archive / nested-folder scanning path: no ZIP test file was available
A downloaded Summary table file: the CSV icon produced no download
The 'Download first well (PNG)' button: it only shows when server-side image export (Kaleido/Chrome) works, so it never appeared
A sample with more than one melt peak, so judging specificity (one product versus several) was only possible by eye on single-peak data
The README's recommended standalone HTML version (all-wells mean ± SD overlay, separate curve/peak Y-axis scaling, combined long PNG): outside this tree's scope (Streamlit app only)
not_done: PNG and PDF export through 'Export all selected wells' failed with 'RuntimeError: Kaleido requires Google Chrome to be installed' (screens/041.webp, screens/042.webp). Only HTML export succeeded. Client-side PNG via the Plotly camera button worked.

'Export all selected wells' writes files to a server temp folder (/work/tmp/qpcr_export_*), not to a browser download, so I could not open those files. I did download and read the combined HTML (melt_plots.html), which contains W1 traces C8 and D8 only (B8 excluded).
Clicking the Summary table's download (CSV) icon produced no download, so I could not obtain the summary table as a file. No kept screen shows this attempt.

Changing the well filter and re-selecting wells cleared the per-well exclusion lists (screens/037.webp, screens/038.webp), and the curve-deviation method did not re-flag automatically after that. I re-entered the exclusion by hand.
A curve_only well shows Replicates 0 in the Summary even though its curve plot shows 3 replicates (screens/055.webp).
The peak Tm deviation outlier method flagged nothing at 0.50 or 0.05 °C (screens/029.webp, screens/030.webp); the replay also found nothing at 0.10 °C. It is not shown to work on this data.
Uploading a ZIP archive or nested folder was not tried: no ZIP test file was available.
I did not check what the Experiment name field is used for (it was not visible in any plot title or in the exports I could read).
